newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine two-year note coupon rate at 11.875 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine two-year note coupon rate at 11.875 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' two-year fixed rate note yielded the same coupon rate as last month's 11.875 percent during the regular auction on Tuesday, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The average rate, however, was lower than last month at 11.775 percent versus 11.738. Rates ranged from 11.624/11.875 percent compared with the previous 11.491/11.875.
The auction generated 6.535 billion pesos worth of tenders, of which four billion pesos were awarded.
Rates were almost steady since the two-year rates had already fallen sharply last month following a cut in reserve requirements, traders said.
"I think rates would have been lower if the Central Bank had not sent feelers it wants rates at these levels," a foreign bank dealer said, citing the high liquidity in the market.
Liquidity has risen because banks have been discouraged from investing in term reverse repos. The instruments now carry a new 20 percent tax.
